diagnosis.statement: The previously separate geometry-type and apparent radius mismatches are not terminal: sharp spherical slicing plus outer-to-inner restriction transforms finite-I capacity into the exact weak-linear geometry at the admissible inner radius, provided a scale-invariant temporal-coherence quantity is small. State-space/ancestry transport remains separate.

nonclaims: No target-domain counterexample rules out NSE dynamics forcing the needed smallness.
No impossibility of a pressure/ancestry/radial-distribution repair is proved.
No Grujic theorem invocation on the ancient state is claimed.
No Navier-Stokes root theorem is obtained.
failure.supported_failure: In the low-zeta branch the sufficient condition is I sqrt(zeta) <= universal(delta,d0); finite I only gives finiteness, not this universal smallness. The registered ancient producer is also not itself the regular pre-singular solution/time pair of Grujic Theorem 4.2.

lesson.statement: A producer radius larger than a consumer radius is not automatically an interface failure when the observation is monotone under restriction. First compare the producer's decay exponent against the radius-ratio penalty, then optimize the outer scale; here A^-4 volume decay before persistence saturation beats the A penalty after the cube-root line transform.

motif.reusable_pattern: outer volume decay -> sharp central-line slicing -> inner restriction -> scale optimization -> dimensionless compatibility coordinate
motif.scope: all-center superlevel capacity bounds with critical inner consumer scale and a persistence cutoff

obstruction.statement: A terminal geometric route now needs a consumer-valid time/state transport plus a dynamic estimate making I sqrt(K/Omega_t^2) universally small (or replacing K by a sharper local temporal coherence carrier); pure volume geometry alone is no longer the first obstruction.
